newsitem.title: USA: Jurors resume deliberations in Army rape case.
newsitem.headline: Jurors resume deliberations in Army rape case.

text.p: Military jurors resumed deliberations Friday in the court martial of Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson, who is accused of raping six female trainees at the Army's Aberdeen Proving Ground.
The six-member jury is trying to decide Simpson's guilt on 19 counts of rape and 35 other charges, including forcible sodomy, indecent assault and maltreatment.
"We feel confident in our case. We've felt confident all along," said Simpson's lead attorney, Frank Spinner, after deliberations began Thursday afternoon.
Testimony in the trial concluded Tuesday after eight days.
Simpson's is the highest profile case in a major sexual misconduct investigation at the base, which has become the military's biggest sexual harassment scandal since the Navy's 1991 Tailhook affair.

Simpson, 32, is the first of 12 trainers charged with various acts of misconduct at Aberdeen to go before a court martial, and he is charged with the most rapes. Four cases have been settled earlier through plea agreements or administrative proceedings, although none has yielded a rape conviction.
In response to the Aberdeen probe, the Army launched an investigation of harassment throughout the service.

In closing arguments Thursday, prosecutor Capt. Theresa Gallagher described Simpson as a "criminal wearing a green uniform," who used his power and authority as a drill instructor to sexually prey on female trainees under his authority.
Spinner said in his arguments that Simpson engaged only in consensual sex.

The attorney argued there was no physical evidence of rape and said all the women he is alleged to have raped had reason to lie, meaning the government had failed to prove his guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.

Simpson has pleaded guilty to 11 counts of consensual sex and five counts of propositioning, for which he faces a total maximum sentence of 32 years in prison. He faces a life sentence if convicted of rape.
Under military rules, a two-thirds vote of the jury -- or four votes in this case -- is required to convict Simpson on any of the charges he faces.
Any lesser vote signifies acquittal on the charge, although the jury can also convict on certain lesser charges involving the same incident.
A sentencing hearing to consider punishment for the crimes Simpson has pleaded guilty to as well as any additional convictions is to immediately follow the verdict.

Simpson is a 13-year veteran of the military, who took up his post as a drill sergeant at Aberdeen in January 1995, and has received decorations including good conduct medals and army achievement medals.
